# What this notebook does

Kate, 2026-10-27: the length densities (`26d_target_cluster_feature_importance.Rmd` section 7)
show eIF3d targets with longer 5'UTRs and shorter CDSs and 3'UTRs. Question: does a gene need a
long 5'UTR **or** a short CDS / 3'UTR (either route suffices), or do the lengths simply add up?

**Predictors** (the matrix's own columns, log2(length + 1)): 5'UTR, CDS and 3'UTR length. Total
length is left out: it is close to their sum, so it would make the coefficients unstable.

**Models**, each fitted twice:

- **linear**: outcome = log2 TE change, log2(sictrl / si3d), every modelled gene. Uses the size
  of each gene's response, no cut-off.
- **logistic**: outcome = eIF3d target yes / no (log2 TE change > 0.5 and padj < 0.05), the
  question as asked.

| model | terms |
|---|---|
| each length alone | 3 models, 1 term each |
| each pair, additive | 5'UTR + CDS, 5'UTR + 3'UTR, CDS + 3'UTR |
| all three, additive | 5'UTR + CDS + 3'UTR |
| all three, multiplicative | 5'UTR x CDS x 3'UTR: the three lengths, the three pairwise products and the triple product |

**Reading the multiplicative model for OR.** In an additive model each length shifts the outcome
by a fixed amount whatever the others are. Under OR, a gene that already qualifies by one route
gains little from the other, so the interaction between a favourable 5'UTR (long) and a
favourable CDS (short) is **sub-additive**. Long 5'UTR raises the outcome and long CDS lowers it,
so OR shows up as a **positive 5'UTR x CDS coefficient**: the benefit of a long 5'UTR shrinks as
the CDS gets shorter. Predictors are centred on their means before multiplying, so the main
effects in that model are the slopes at an average gene.

**Section 4** is the model-free version: genes binned into length quintiles, the fraction that are
targets in each cell, and how far each cell sits from what the additive logistic model predicts.

**Same genes in every model**: modelled genes with all three lengths, so fits are comparable.
Fit is reported as adjusted R² (linear) or AUC (logistic), both in-sample and 10-fold
cross-validated; the cross-validated numbers are out-of-sample and not adjusted.

```{r libraries}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(tidyverse); library(here); library(patchwork) })
O <- here("output", "translational_control_overview")
SAVE <- isTRUE(params$save_plots)
div <- c("#0072B2", "white", "#D55E00")
```

# 1. Data and checks

```{r data}
oof <- readRDS(file.path(O, paste0("shap_oof_", params$suffix, ".rds")))
de <- read_csv(here("output", params$de_file), show_col_types = FALSE) %>% mutate(gene_id_clean = sub("[.].*", "", gene_id))
# Direction: the siRNA depletes its own target, so EIF3D mRNA must be strongly positive under log2(sictrl / si3d)
kd <- de$rna_lfc[de$symbol == "EIF3D"]
stopifnot("EIF3D not found once" = length(kd) == 1,
          "EIF3D rna_lfc not strongly positive: direction flipped or wrong knockdown" = kd > 1,
          "modelled genes missing from the DE file" = all(oof$genes$gene_id_clean %in% de$gene_id_clean),
          "outcome differs from the DE file's te_lfc" =
            max(abs(oof$genes$y - de$te_lfc[match(oof$genes$gene_id_clean, de$gene_id_clean)])) < 1e-12)
cat(sprintf("EIF3D rna_lfc %+.2f -> log2(sictrl / si3d) confirmed; outcome = %s te_lfc\n", kd, params$de_file))

fm <- readRDS(file.path(O, params$matrix_rds))
stopifnot("matrix has duplicate genes" = !anyDuplicated(fm$gene_id_clean))
len_cols <- c(utr5 = "log2_utr5_length", cds = "log2_cds_length", utr3 = "log2_utr3_length")
d0 <- oof$genes %>% transmute(gene_id_clean, symbol, te_lfc = y, te_padj = y_padj, target = set == params$set_label) %>%
  bind_cols(fm[match(oof$genes$gene_id_clean, fm$gene_id_clean), unname(len_cols)] %>%
              mutate(across(everything(), ~ as.numeric(unlist(.x)))) %>% setNames(names(len_cols)))
stopifnot("target label does not follow its rule" = identical(d0$target, d0$te_lfc > 0.5 & d0$te_padj < 0.05 & !is.na(d0$te_padj)),
          "lengths out of range" = all(d0$cds > 0, na.rm = TRUE) && all(d0$utr5 >= 0, na.rm = TRUE) && all(d0$utr3 >= 0, na.rm = TRUE),
          "ACTB CDS is not 1,128 nt" = abs(2^d0$cds[d0$symbol == "ACTB"] - 1 - 1128) < 1e-6)
d <- d0 %>% filter(!is.na(utr5), !is.na(cds), !is.na(utr3)) %>% arrange(gene_id_clean)   # fixed order for CV folds
cat(sprintf("modelled genes %s; with all three lengths %s (dropped %d missing a length); targets %d\n",
            scales::comma(nrow(d0)), scales::comma(nrow(d)), nrow(d0) - nrow(d), sum(d$target)))
knitr::kable(tibble(length = names(len_cols),
                    rho_with_log2_te_change = map_dbl(names(len_cols), ~ cor(d[[.x]], d$te_lfc, method = "spearman")),
                    median_nt_targets = map_dbl(names(len_cols), ~ median(2^d[[.x]][d$target] - 1)),
                    median_nt_others = map_dbl(names(len_cols), ~ median(2^d[[.x]][!d$target] - 1))),
             digits = 3, caption = "each length: Spearman rho with log2 TE change, and median length (nt)")
knitr::kable(round(cor(d[, names(len_cols)], method = "spearman"), 3), caption = "Spearman rho between the lengths")
```

# 2. The models

```{r fit}
# centred copies, so main effects in the multiplicative model are slopes at an average gene
dc <- d %>% mutate(across(all_of(names(len_cols)), ~ .x - mean(.x)))
forms <- c("5'UTR alone" = "utr5", "CDS alone" = "cds", "3'UTR alone" = "utr3",
           "5'UTR + CDS" = "utr5 + cds", "5'UTR + 3'UTR" = "utr5 + utr3", "CDS + 3'UTR" = "cds + utr3",
           "5'UTR + CDS + 3'UTR" = "utr5 + cds + utr3",
           "5'UTR x CDS x 3'UTR" = "utr5 * cds * utr3")
auc <- function(score, y) { r <- rank(score); n1 <- sum(y); n0 <- sum(!y); (sum(r[y]) - n1 * (n1 + 1) / 2) / (n1 * n0) }
set.seed(9); fold <- sample(rep(1:10, length.out = nrow(dc)))
fit_one <- function(rhs) {
  f_lin <- as.formula(paste("te_lfc ~", rhs)); f_log <- as.formula(paste("target ~", rhs))
  m_lin <- lm(f_lin, data = dc); m_log <- glm(f_log, data = dc, family = binomial)
  cv_lin <- cv_log <- numeric(nrow(dc))
  for (k in 1:10) {
    tr <- dc[fold != k, ]; te <- dc[fold == k, ]
    cv_lin[fold == k] <- predict(lm(f_lin, data = tr), te)
    cv_log[fold == k] <- predict(glm(f_log, data = tr, family = binomial), te)   # link scale is enough for AUC
  }
  list(lin = m_lin, log = m_log,
       row = tibble(n_terms = length(coef(m_lin)) - 1,
                    adj_r2 = summary(m_lin)$adj.r.squared,
                    cv_r2 = 1 - sum((dc$te_lfc - cv_lin)^2) / sum((dc$te_lfc - mean(dc$te_lfc))^2),
                    aic_linear = AIC(m_lin),
                    auc = auc(predict(m_log), dc$target), cv_auc = auc(cv_log, dc$target),
                    aic_logistic = AIC(m_log)))
}
fits <- map(forms, fit_one)
tab <- imap_dfr(fits, ~ .x$row %>% mutate(model = .y, .before = 1))
stopifnot("in-sample R2 must not fall when a term is added to a nested model" =
            tab$adj_r2[tab$model == "5'UTR x CDS x 3'UTR"] >= tab$adj_r2[tab$model == "5'UTR + CDS + 3'UTR"] - 0.001,
          "AUC outside [0, 1]" = all(between(tab$auc, 0, 1)),
          "single-length R2 must equal r^2" =
            abs(summary(fits[["CDS alone"]]$lin)$r.squared - cor(dc$cds, dc$te_lfc)^2) < 1e-10)
knitr::kable(tab, digits = c(0, 0, 4, 4, 0, 3, 3, 0),
             caption = sprintf("fit of each model, n = %s genes (%d targets). Linear: log2 TE change. Logistic: target yes/no.",
                               scales::comma(nrow(dc)), sum(dc$target)))
```

## Does each length add to the others? (nested tests)

```{r nested}
nest <- tribble(~smaller, ~larger,
  "5'UTR + CDS", "5'UTR + CDS + 3'UTR", "5'UTR + 3'UTR", "5'UTR + CDS + 3'UTR", "CDS + 3'UTR", "5'UTR + CDS + 3'UTR",
  "5'UTR + CDS + 3'UTR", "5'UTR x CDS x 3'UTR")
nest_tab <- nest %>% mutate(
  adds = c("3'UTR", "CDS", "5'UTR", "the four interaction terms"),
  adj_r2_gain = map2_dbl(smaller, larger, ~ tab$adj_r2[tab$model == .y] - tab$adj_r2[tab$model == .x]),
  F_p_linear = map2_dbl(smaller, larger, ~ anova(fits[[.x]]$lin, fits[[.y]]$lin)$`Pr(>F)`[2]),
  cv_auc_gain = map2_dbl(smaller, larger, ~ tab$cv_auc[tab$model == .y] - tab$cv_auc[tab$model == .x]),
  LRT_p_logistic = map2_dbl(smaller, larger, ~ anova(fits[[.x]]$log, fits[[.y]]$log, test = "LRT")$`Pr(>Chi)`[2]))
knitr::kable(nest_tab, digits = c(0, 0, 0, 4, 300, 4, 300))
```

## Coefficients: additive and multiplicative

Linear coefficients are the change in log2 TE change per doubling of that length (predictors
are log2, so one unit = a doubling); logistic coefficients are the change in log-odds of being a
target per doubling. In the multiplicative model, main effects are at the average of the other
lengths (centred predictors).

```{r coefs}
coef_tab <- function(m, kind) {
  s <- summary(m)$coefficients; ci <- suppressMessages(confint.default(m))
  tibble(term = rownames(s), estimate = s[, 1], lo = ci[, 1], hi = ci[, 2], p = s[, 4]) %>%
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
    mutate(term = str_replace_all(term, c("utr5" = "5'UTR", "cds" = "CDS", "utr3" = "3'UTR", ":" = " x ")),
           model = kind)
}
coefs <- bind_rows(coef_tab(fits[["5'UTR + CDS + 3'UTR"]]$lin, "linear, additive"),
                   coef_tab(fits[["5'UTR x CDS x 3'UTR"]]$lin, "linear, multiplicative"),
                   coef_tab(fits[["5'UTR + CDS + 3'UTR"]]$log, "logistic, additive"),
                   coef_tab(fits[["5'UTR x CDS x 3'UTR"]]$log, "logistic, multiplicative"))
knitr::kable(coefs %>% dplyr::select(model, everything()), digits = c(0, 0, 4, 4, 4, 300))
ix <- coefs %>% filter(term == "5'UTR x CDS")
cat(sprintf("5'UTR x CDS interaction: linear %+.4f (p = %.2g) | logistic %+.4f (p = %.2g). Positive = sub-additive = the OR pattern.\n",
            ix$estimate[1], ix$p[1], ix$estimate[2], ix$p[2]))
if (SAVE) {
  write_csv(tab, file.path(O, "length_models_fit_hypoxia_1hr.csv"))
  write_csv(coefs, file.path(O, "length_models_coefficients_hypoxia_1hr.csv"))
}
```

## Figure: fit and coefficients

Left: how much of log2 TE change each model explains. Right: each linear model's coefficients,
the change in log2 TE change per **doubling** of that length (predictors are log2), with 95%
confidence intervals. In the multiplicative model these are the main effects at an average gene
(centred predictors); its interaction terms are in the coefficient table above.

```{r fig_models, fig.width = 13, fig.height = 5.5}
tl <- tab %>% dplyr::select(model, adj_r2, cv_r2) %>% mutate(model = factor(model, levels = rev(names(forms))))
p_r2 <- ggplot(tl, aes(y = model)) +
  geom_col(aes(x = adj_r2), fill = "grey75", width = 0.6) +
  geom_point(aes(x = cv_r2), colour = "black", size = 2) +
  labs(x = "adjusted R² (bar); 10-fold CV R² (point)", y = NULL, title = "fit: log2 TE change") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
term_lab <- c(utr5 = "5'UTR", cds = "CDS", utr3 = "3'UTR")
betas <- imap_dfr(fits, function(f, nm) {
  s <- summary(f$lin)$coefficients; ci <- confint(f$lin)
  tibble(model = nm, term = rownames(s), estimate = s[, 1], lo = ci[, 1], hi = ci[, 2])
}) %>% filter(term %in% names(term_lab)) %>%
  mutate(term = factor(term_lab[term], levels = term_lab),
         model = factor(model, levels = levels(tl$model)))
p_beta <- ggplot(betas, aes(estimate, model, colour = term)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), size = 0.3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`5'UTR` = "#009E73", CDS = "#0072B2", `3'UTR` = "#CC79A7"), name = "length") +
  scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "coefficient: change in log2 TE change per doubling (95% CI)", y = NULL, title = "linear coefficients") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank())
p_mod <- p_r2 + p_beta + plot_annotation(
  title = sprintf("%s: how much do the three lengths explain log2 TE change?", params$label),
  subtitle = sprintf("log2 5'UTR, CDS and 3'UTR length; n = %s genes",
                     scales::comma(nrow(dc))))
p_mod
if (SAVE) ggsave(here("plots", "37_length_models_fit_hypoxia_1hr.pdf"), p_mod, width = 13, height = 5.5)
```

# 3. The model-free check: target fraction across length quintiles

Each pair of lengths, genes binned into `r params$n_bins` equal-count bins on each axis
(quintiles of all modelled genes), giving `r params$n_bins^2` cells.

- **Left:** fraction of the cell's genes that are targets (and n).
- **Right:** that fraction minus the mean prediction of the **additive** logistic model (all three
  lengths) for the same genes, in percentage points. An additive model fits this cell where it
  is white. Under OR, the corner where both lengths are favourable sits **below** the additive
  prediction (blue): having both adds less than additive odds expect.

Overall target fraction: `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(d$target))`.

```{r grid, fig.width = 13, fig.height = 5.5, results = "asis"}
dc$pred_add <- predict(fits[["5'UTR + CDS + 3'UTR"]]$log, type = "response")
q_lab <- function(x, n) {
  br <- unique(quantile(x, seq(0, 1, length.out = n + 1)))
  cut(x, br, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = sprintf("%s-%s", scales::comma(round(2^head(br, -1) - 1)), scales::comma(round(2^br[-1] - 1))))
}
lab_nt <- c(utr5 = "5'UTR length (nt)", cds = "CDS length (nt)", utr3 = "3'UTR length (nt)")
grid_tabs <- list()
for (pp in list(c("cds", "utr5"), c("cds", "utr3"), c("utr3", "utr5"))) {
  gx <- pp[1]; gy <- pp[2]
  g <- d %>% mutate(bx = q_lab(.data[[gx]], params$n_bins), by = q_lab(.data[[gy]], params$n_bins), pred = dc$pred_add) %>%
    group_by(bx, by) %>% summarise(n = n(), frac = mean(target), expected = mean(pred), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(diff_pp = 100 * (frac - expected))
  stopifnot("cells do not add up to the genes" = sum(g$n) == nrow(d))
  grid_tabs[[paste(gy, "vs", gx)]] <- g %>% mutate(x = gx, y = gy)
  lim <- max(abs(g$diff_pp))
  p1 <- ggplot(g, aes(bx, by, fill = 100 * frac)) + geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%\nn = %d", 100 * frac, n)), size = 2.8) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#E69F00", name = "targets (%)") +
    labs(x = sprintf("log2 bins: %s", lab_nt[gx]), y = sprintf("log2 bins: %s", lab_nt[gy]), title = "observed target fraction") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
  p2 <- ggplot(g, aes(bx, by, fill = diff_pp)) + geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%+.1f", diff_pp)), size = 3) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = div[1], mid = div[2], high = div[3], limits = c(-lim, lim), name = "observed -\nadditive (pp)") +
    labs(x = sprintf("log2 bins: %s", lab_nt[gx]), y = NULL, title = "observed minus additive-model prediction") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
  p <- p1 + p2 + plot_annotation(
    title = sprintf("%s: eIF3d targets by %s and %s", params$label, sub(" [(]nt[)]", "", lab_nt[gy]), sub(" [(]nt[)]", "", lab_nt[gx])),
    subtitle = sprintf("quintile bins of all modelled genes (n = %s, %d targets, %.1f%% overall); additive model = logistic on all three log2 lengths",
                       scales::comma(nrow(d)), sum(d$target), 100 * mean(d$target)))
  cat("\n\n## ", sub(" [(]nt[)]", "", lab_nt[gy]), " vs ", sub(" [(]nt[)]", "", lab_nt[gx]), "\n\n", sep = ""); print(p)
  if (SAVE) ggsave(here("plots", sprintf("37_target_fraction_grid_%s_vs_%s_hypoxia_1hr.pdf", gy, gx)), p, width = 13, height = 5.5)
}
if (SAVE) write_csv(bind_rows(grid_tabs), file.path(O, "length_grid_target_fraction_hypoxia_1hr.csv"))
```

## 5'UTR x CDS at finer resolution

The observed target fraction for 5'UTR vs CDS length alone, in `r params$n_bins_fine` equal-count
bins per axis (deciles of all modelled genes), so roughly `r round(nrow(d) / params$n_bins_fine^2)`
genes per cell. Cells this small are noisy: at a 14% base rate and n = 100 a cell's standard
error is about 3.5 percentage points.

```{r grid_fine, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 9}
gf <- d %>% mutate(bx = q_lab(cds, params$n_bins_fine), by = q_lab(utr5, params$n_bins_fine)) %>%
  group_by(bx, by) %>% summarise(n = n(), frac = mean(target), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot("cells do not add up to the genes" = sum(gf$n) == nrow(d),
          "decile bins collapsed - tied lengths" = n_distinct(gf$bx) == params$n_bins_fine && n_distinct(gf$by) == params$n_bins_fine)
p_fine <- ggplot(gf, aes(bx, by, fill = 100 * frac)) + geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%\nn = %d", 100 * frac, n)), size = 2.6) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#E69F00", name = "targets (%)") +
  labs(x = "CDS length (nt), decile bins", y = "5'UTR length (nt), decile bins",
       title = sprintf("%s: eIF3d targets by 5'UTR and CDS length", params$label),
       subtitle = sprintf("observed fraction of targets per cell; deciles of all modelled genes (n = %s, %d targets, %.1f%% overall)",
                          scales::comma(nrow(d)), sum(d$target), 100 * mean(d$target))) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
p_fine
if (SAVE) ggsave(here("plots", sprintf("37_target_fraction_grid_utr5_vs_cds_%dbins_hypoxia_1hr.pdf", params$n_bins_fine)),
                 p_fine, width = 11, height = 9)
```

## GC3 x CDS at the same resolution

The same plot with **GC3** in place of 5'UTR length: `gc3_internal`, GC at the third codon
position with the start and stop codons removed (the corrected variant the model uses). Same
genes, same CDS deciles.

```{r grid_fine_gc3, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 9}
d$gc3 <- as.numeric(unlist(fm$gc3_internal[match(d$gene_id_clean, fm$gene_id_clean)]))
stopifnot("GC3 outside [0, 100]" = all(d$gc3 >= 0 & d$gc3 <= 100, na.rm = TRUE),
          "GC3 median outside 40-65%" = between(median(d$gc3, na.rm = TRUE), 40, 65))
dg <- d %>% filter(!is.na(gc3))
q_lab_pct <- function(x, n) {
  br <- unique(quantile(x, seq(0, 1, length.out = n + 1)))
  cut(x, br, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = sprintf("%.1f-%.1f", head(br, -1), br[-1]))
}
gg <- dg %>% mutate(bx = q_lab(cds, params$n_bins_fine), by = q_lab_pct(gc3, params$n_bins_fine)) %>%
  group_by(bx, by) %>% summarise(n = n(), frac = mean(target), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot("cells do not add up to the genes" = sum(gg$n) == nrow(dg),
          "decile bins collapsed" = n_distinct(gg$bx) == params$n_bins_fine && n_distinct(gg$by) == params$n_bins_fine)
cat(sprintf("genes with GC3: %s of %s; Spearman rho(GC3, log2 CDS length) = %.3f\n", scales::comma(nrow(dg)),
            scales::comma(nrow(d)), cor(dg$gc3, dg$cds, method = "spearman")))
p_gc3 <- ggplot(gg, aes(bx, by, fill = 100 * frac)) + geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%\nn = %d", 100 * frac, n)), size = 2.6) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#E69F00", name = "targets (%)") +
  labs(x = "CDS length (nt), decile bins", y = "GC3 (%), decile bins",
       title = sprintf("%s: eIF3d targets by GC3 and CDS length", params$label),
       subtitle = sprintf("observed fraction of targets per cell; deciles of all modelled genes (n = %s, %d targets, %.1f%% overall)",
                          scales::comma(nrow(dg)), sum(dg$target), 100 * mean(dg$target))) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
p_gc3
if (SAVE) ggsave(here("plots", sprintf("37_target_fraction_grid_gc3_vs_cds_%dbins_hypoxia_1hr.pdf", params$n_bins_fine)),
                 p_gc3, width = 11, height = 9)
```

# 4. Lengths plus GC

Kate, 2026-10-27: the three log2 lengths plus GC of each region (5'UTR, CDS, 3'UTR) and GC3
(`gc3_internal`), seven predictors, outcome log2 TE change. Fitted two ways:

- **additive**: 7 terms.
- **multiplicative**: all seven multiplied together, i.e. every interaction up to the seven-way
  product, 127 terms. Cross-validated R² shows whether that many terms overfit.

The lengths-only models from section 2 and a GC-only model (four GC terms, additive) are refit
here as reference rows. Same genes and the same 10 folds as section 2.

**Predictors are z-scored** (mean 0, SD 1) in this section, so coefficients on GC (%) and on log2
length share one scale: change in log2 TE change **per SD** of the predictor. In the
multiplicative model these are main effects at an average gene.

**CDS GC and GC3 are near-duplicates** (Spearman rho 0.93), and 3'UTR GC tracks both (~0.75).
Their individual coefficients are unstable and split credit between them; the variance inflation
factors below say how much. Read the GC block's coefficients together, not one at a time.

```{r gc_models}
pred7 <- c(utr5 = "log2 5'UTR length", cds = "log2 CDS length", utr3 = "log2 3'UTR length",
           utr5_gc = "5'UTR GC", cds_gc = "CDS GC", utr3_gc = "3'UTR GC", gc3 = "GC3")
dz <- d %>% mutate(utr5_gc = as.numeric(unlist(fm$utr5_gc[match(gene_id_clean, fm$gene_id_clean)])),
                   cds_gc = as.numeric(unlist(fm$cds_gc[match(gene_id_clean, fm$gene_id_clean)])),
                   utr3_gc = as.numeric(unlist(fm$utr3_gc[match(gene_id_clean, fm$gene_id_clean)])))
stopifnot("a predictor has missing values on the section 2 genes" = !anyNA(dz[, names(pred7)]),
          "GC outside [0, 100]" = all(as.matrix(dz[, c("utr5_gc", "cds_gc", "utr3_gc", "gc3")]) >= 0 &
                                        as.matrix(dz[, c("utr5_gc", "cds_gc", "utr3_gc", "gc3")]) <= 100),
          "ACTB CDS GC outside 50-70%" = between(dz$cds_gc[dz$symbol == "ACTB"], 50, 70),
          "genes or order differ from section 2, so the folds would not match" = identical(dz$gene_id_clean, dc$gene_id_clean))
dz <- dz %>% mutate(across(all_of(names(pred7)), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x))))

# variance inflation: 1 / (1 - R2 of each predictor on the other six)
vif <- sapply(names(pred7), function(p) 1 / (1 - summary(lm(reformulate(setdiff(names(pred7), p), p), data = dz))$r.squared))
knitr::kable(tibble(predictor = pred7, VIF = vif), digits = 2,
             caption = "variance inflation factor (1 = independent of the others; > 5 = coefficient poorly determined)")

forms_gc <- c("3 lengths, additive" = "utr5 + cds + utr3",
              "3 lengths, multiplicative" = "utr5 * cds * utr3",
              "4 GC, additive" = "utr5_gc + cds_gc + utr3_gc + gc3",
              "lengths + GC, additive" = paste(names(pred7), collapse = " + "),
              "lengths + GC, multiplicative" = paste(names(pred7), collapse = " * "))
fit_lin_cv <- function(rhs) {
  f <- as.formula(paste("te_lfc ~", rhs)); m <- lm(f, data = dz)
  cv <- numeric(nrow(dz))
  for (k in 1:10) cv[fold == k] <- predict(lm(f, data = dz[fold != k, ]), dz[fold == k, ])
  list(m = m, row = tibble(n_terms = length(coef(m)) - 1, adj_r2 = summary(m)$adj.r.squared,
                           cv_r2 = 1 - sum((dz$te_lfc - cv)^2) / sum((dz$te_lfc - mean(dz$te_lfc))^2), aic = AIC(m)))
}
fits_gc <- map(forms_gc, fit_lin_cv)
tab_gc <- imap_dfr(fits_gc, ~ .x$row %>% mutate(model = .y, .before = 1))
stopifnot("multiplicative model should have 127 terms" = tab_gc$n_terms[tab_gc$model == "lengths + GC, multiplicative"] == 127,
          "lengths-only rows must reproduce section 2 (z-scoring does not change fit)" =
            abs(tab_gc$adj_r2[1] - tab$adj_r2[tab$model == "5'UTR + CDS + 3'UTR"]) < 1e-10 &&
            abs(tab_gc$cv_r2[2] - tab$cv_r2[tab$model == "5'UTR x CDS x 3'UTR"]) < 1e-10)
knitr::kable(tab_gc, digits = c(0, 0, 4, 4, 0), caption = sprintf("log2 TE change, n = %s genes, same 10 folds", scales::comma(nrow(dz))))

nest_gc <- tribble(~smaller, ~larger, ~adds,
  "3 lengths, additive", "lengths + GC, additive", "the four GC terms, to the lengths",
  "4 GC, additive", "lengths + GC, additive", "the three lengths, to GC",
  "lengths + GC, additive", "lengths + GC, multiplicative", "all 120 interaction terms") %>%
  mutate(adj_r2_gain = map2_dbl(smaller, larger, ~ tab_gc$adj_r2[tab_gc$model == .y] - tab_gc$adj_r2[tab_gc$model == .x]),
         cv_r2_gain = map2_dbl(smaller, larger, ~ tab_gc$cv_r2[tab_gc$model == .y] - tab_gc$cv_r2[tab_gc$model == .x]),
         F_p = map2_dbl(smaller, larger, ~ anova(fits_gc[[.x]]$m, fits_gc[[.y]]$m)$`Pr(>F)`[2]))
knitr::kable(nest_gc, digits = c(0, 0, 0, 4, 4, 300))

coef_gc <- bind_rows(
  imap_dfr(fits_gc[c("lengths + GC, additive", "lengths + GC, multiplicative")], function(f, nm) {
    s <- summary(f$m)$coefficients; ci <- confint(f$m)
    tibble(model = nm, term = rownames(s), estimate = s[, 1], lo = ci[, 1], hi = ci[, 2], t = s[, 3], p = s[, 4])
  })) %>% filter(term != "(Intercept)")
knitr::kable(coef_gc %>% filter(term %in% names(pred7)) %>% mutate(term = pred7[term]), digits = c(0, 0, 4, 4, 4, 1, 300),
             caption = "main effects, change in log2 TE change per SD")
knitr::kable(coef_gc %>% filter(model == "lengths + GC, multiplicative", !term %in% names(pred7)) %>%
               arrange(desc(abs(t))) %>% head(10) %>%
               mutate(term = map_chr(strsplit(term, ":", fixed = TRUE), ~ paste(pred7[.x], collapse = " x "))),
             digits = c(0, 0, 4, 4, 4, 1, 300), caption = "the 10 largest interaction terms by |t| (of 120)")
if (SAVE) {
  write_csv(tab_gc, file.path(O, "length_gc_models_fit_hypoxia_1hr.csv"))
  write_csv(coef_gc, file.path(O, "length_gc_models_coefficients_hypoxia_1hr.csv"))
}
```

```{r fig_gc_models, fig.width = 13, fig.height = 5.5}
tg_ <- tab_gc %>% mutate(model = factor(model, levels = rev(names(forms_gc))))
p_r2g <- ggplot(tg_, aes(y = model)) +
  geom_col(aes(x = adj_r2), fill = "grey75", width = 0.6) +
  geom_point(aes(x = cv_r2), colour = "black", size = 2) +
  geom_text(aes(x = adj_r2, label = sprintf("%d terms", n_terms)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.3))) +
  labs(x = "adjusted R² (bar); cross-validated R², 10-fold (point)", y = NULL, title = "fit: log2 TE change") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
bg <- coef_gc %>% filter(term %in% names(pred7)) %>%
  mutate(term = factor(pred7[term], levels = rev(pred7)),
         model = recode(model, "lengths + GC, additive" = "additive", "lengths + GC, multiplicative" = "multiplicative (main effects)"))
p_bg <- ggplot(bg, aes(estimate, term, colour = model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), size = 0.3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(additive = "black", `multiplicative (main effects)` = "#CC79A7"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "coefficient: change in log2 TE change per SD (95% CI)", y = NULL, title = "lengths + GC: coefficients") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
p_gcm <- p_r2g + p_bg + plot_annotation(
  title = sprintf("%s: log2 TE change on lengths and GC", params$label),
  subtitle = sprintf("log2 5'UTR, CDS and 3'UTR length; GC of each region; GC3. Predictors z-scored; n = %s genes", scales::comma(nrow(dz))))
p_gcm
if (SAVE) ggsave(here("plots", "37_length_gc_models_hypoxia_1hr.pdf"), p_gcm, width = 13, height = 5.5)
```

# 5. Scatters: GC3, 5'UTR length and their ratio against TE change

Kate, 2026-10-27. Every modelled gene with a GC3 and a 5'UTR length, y = log2 TE change
(log2(sictrl / si3d)), all genes in grey with no target colouring. The black
line is a least-squares linear fit over all genes (95% CI band); the stats are Spearman rho, the fitted slope and adjusted R2. Three x axes:

- **GC3** (`gc3_internal`, %).
- **log2 5'UTR length** (log2(nt + 1), as stored in the matrix).
- **log2(GC3 / 5'UTR length)** = log2 GC3 - log2(5'UTR nt + 1). The two point in opposite
  directions (higher GC3 -> lower TE change, longer 5'UTR -> higher), so a low ratio should mark
  the most eIF3d-dependent genes. Taken on the log2 scale because the raw ratio is dominated by
  1 / length: 5'UTR length spans ~1,000-fold, GC3 about 3-fold.

Targets are not coloured: they are defined by TE change > 0.5, so colouring them only marks a
horizontal band by construction; the trend is in the whole cloud.

```{r te_scatters, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6, results = "asis"}
ds <- d0 %>% mutate(gc3 = as.numeric(unlist(fm$gc3_internal[match(gene_id_clean, fm$gene_id_clean)])),
                    ratio = log2(gc3) - utr5) %>%
  filter(!is.na(gc3), !is.na(utr5))
stopifnot("GC3 outside [0, 100]" = all(ds$gc3 >= 0 & ds$gc3 <= 100),
          "GC3 of 0 makes the ratio infinite" = all(is.finite(ds$ratio)))
xs <- list(gc3   = list(lab = "GC3 (%)", file = "gc3"),
           utr5  = list(lab = "log2 5'UTR length", file = "utr5_length"),
           ratio = list(lab = "log2(GC3 / 5'UTR length)", file = "gc3_over_utr5_length"))
# y zoomed to the central 99.8% of genes so a handful of extreme genes do not flatten the cloud;
# the fit and rho still use every gene (coord_cartesian does not drop data)
ylim <- quantile(ds$te_lfc, c(0.001, 0.999))
n_off <- sum(ds$te_lfc < ylim[1] | ds$te_lfc > ylim[2])
for (v in names(xs)) {
  rho <- cor(ds[[v]], ds$te_lfc, method = "spearman")
  fit <- summary(lm(ds$te_lfc ~ ds[[v]]))
  cat(sprintf("\n\n%s: slope %.4f, adjusted R2 %.3f; y zoomed, %d genes off-scale (still in the fit)\n",
              xs[[v]]$lab, coef(fit)[2, 1], fit$adj.r.squared, n_off))
  p <- ggplot(ds, aes(.data[[v]], te_lfc)) +
    geom_point(colour = "grey70", size = 0.5, alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.8, se = TRUE) +
    annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.4, size = 3.6,
             label = sprintf("Spearman rho = %.3f\nn = %s genes", rho, scales::comma(nrow(ds)))) +
    labs(x = xs[[v]]$lab, y = "log2 TE change (sictrl / si3d)",
         title = params$label, subtitle = "all modelled genes; line = linear fit (95% CI)") +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = ylim) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12)
  cat("\n\n## ", xs[[v]]$lab, "\n\n", sep = ""); print(p)
  if (SAVE) ggsave(here("plots", sprintf("37_te_change_vs_%s_hypoxia_1hr.pdf", xs[[v]]$file)), p, width = 7, height = 6)
}
```
